subsystems.name: Exposure carrier
subsystems.role: holds sample trays outside the vehicle, where nothing shields them from vacuum, ultraviolet and cosmic rays.
parts: attachment interface for the host platform

subsystems.name: Sample windows
subsystems.role: let ultraviolet through to the organisms while keeping them sealed and, in some cells, keep light out as a dark control.

subsystems.name: Dosimetry
subsystems.role: measures what the samples actually received, not what the orbit should have given them.

subsystems.name: Recovery and return chain
subsystems.role: brings the samples back without letting contamination or ordinary warmth change the result.
parts: sample-return capsule or crewed return vehicle

subsystems.name: Ground reference lab
subsystems.role: runs the paired control experiment and analyses what came back.
parts: space-simulation vacuum chamber with ultraviolet lamps

buildSteps.title: Define the question
buildSteps.detail: Panspermia, forward-contamination risk and life-detection limits each need different organisms, doses and controls, so the target is stated first.

buildSteps.title: Prepare the samples
buildSteps.detail: Spores, lichens, biofilms or dried cells are grown, counted, dried onto carriers and split into flight, ground-control and dark-control groups.

buildSteps.title: Baseline characterisation
buildSteps.detail: Every sample is fingerprinted before launch — cell counts, vitality, and spectroscopic signatures — so later change can be attributed to space.

buildSteps.title: Package the hardware
buildSteps.detail: Samples go into sealed cells behind ultraviolet-transparent windows, separated from each other so cross-contamination cannot occur.

buildSteps.title: Install outside the vehicle
buildSteps.detail: Trays are mounted on an external platform by spacewalk or robot arm, alongside dosimeters and temperature sensors.

buildSteps.title: Expose
buildSteps.detail: The samples sit in vacuum and full solar ultraviolet for months to years; the dark controls measure the contribution of radiation alone.

buildSteps.title: Retrieve and return
buildSteps.detail: The trays are pulled back inside and flown home, then opened in a laboratory under conditions that keep the surviving cells alive.

buildSteps.title: Assay survival
buildSteps.detail: Colony counts, germination and deoxyribonucleic-acid repair measurements give a survival fraction against the measured dose.

buildSteps.title: Model and extrapolate
buildSteps.detail: Survival data plus dosimetry and environmental records bound how long organisms could ride between planets and how hard spacecraft must be cleaned.

prerequisites.tech: Routine access to external orbital platforms
prerequisites.why: the experiment only works if samples can be left outside a spacecraft and later reached again.
survivors must be counted in a full laboratory; instruments on orbit cannot measure viability well enough.
without a dose record, survival results cannot be compared between flights or extrapolated to other orbits.
separating vacuum, ultraviolet and radiation effects requires the same sample types tested one variable at a time on the ground.
the experiment doubles as a contamination study, so the samples themselves must be known and controlled.

pathway.milestone: external exposure platforms in low Earth orbit, with results from spore, lichen and radio-tolerant bacteria samples
pathway.unlocks: hard numbers on how long a cell can survive in space, and how much shielding a spacecraft needs.

pathway.milestone: exposures outside the Earth's magnetic field, on free-flying or lunar-orbiting carriers
pathway.unlocks: real galactic-cosmic-ray and solar-particle doses rather than the partly shielded low-orbit case.

pathway.milestone: multi-species biofilms and communities tested inside regolith and brine analogues
pathway.unlocks: understanding of whether ecosystems, not just single hardy cells, can persist.

pathway.milestone: results feeding directly into planetary-protection rules and habitat shielding design for crewed deep-space missions
pathway.unlocks: safer Mars sample return and life-detection missions that can still recognise a false positive.
